summary: This defensive disclosure compiles concrete therapeutic protocols, molecular identifiers, SCAP target mechanisms, and patent landscape analysis for the senolytic combination of dasatinib and quercetin (D+Q). The document cites foundational peer-reviewed studies accurately and dedicates the synthesis to the public domain under CC0 1.0 to establish prior art against downstream method-of-use claims. It fulfills all criteria for an enabling defensive publication.
strengths: Provides enabling clinical and pharmacological details including CAS numbers, IUPAC names, molecular formulas, oral dosing ranges (dasatinib 100 mg/day, quercetin 1000–1250 mg/day), and intermittent administration schedules.

Features exceptionally accurate and verified prior-art citations across preclinical discovery (Zhu et al. 2015), human pilot trials (Justice et al. 2019, Hickson et al. 2019, Nambiar et al. 2023), and relevant patent filings (US11517572B2, WO2015116740A1).
Presents a rigorous analysis of the complementary mechanism of action across distinct cell types and SCAP nodes (SRC/ephrin vs. PI3K/BCL-2/serpines).
Contains an explicit CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication and balanced limitations regarding safety, bioavailability, and small pilot sample sizes.
weaknesses: Relies solely on published literature without proposing novel synthetic formulation strategies or excipient combinations that could overcome quercetin's poor oral bioavailability.
Does not discuss potential differences in tissue pharmacokinetics between oral Sprycel tablets and varied over-the-counter quercetin preparations.
suggestions: Detail specific oral lipid-based or phytosome delivery methods for quercetin to further strengthen enabling prior art on formulation bioavailability.
Include a brief discussion of monitoring parameters (e.g., CBC for dasatinib-induced cytopenias) to enhance clinical reproducibility.

claims.text: Dasatinib selectively killed senescent preadipocytes; quercetin selectively killed senescent HUVECs and BM-MSCs; the combination was effective against both cell types.

A two-center, open-label study of intermittent DQ (D:100 mg/day, Q:1250 mg/day, three-days/week over three-weeks) was conducted in participants with IPF (n = 14) to evaluate feasibility of implementing a senolytic intervention.

Adipose tissue macrophages, which are attracted, anchored, and activated by senescent cells, and crown-like structures were decreased. Skin epidermal p16INK4A+ and p21CIP1+ cells were reduced, as were circulating SASP factors, including IL-1α, IL-6, and MMPs-9 and -12.

US Patent US11517572B2. 'Killing senescent cells and treating senescence-associated conditions using a Src inhibitor and a flavonoid.' Granted December 6, 2022 (priority January 28, 2014). Assignee: Mayo Foundation for Medical Education and Research.
